chunks.title: No Accounts, No Telemetry, No Analytics
chunks.text: No Accounts, No Telemetry, No Analytics. Settings surfaces the claim: "Dictation stays on your iPhone. Ask and long rewrites use Apple's Private Cloud Compute — end-to-end encrypted, never stored. No accounts, no telemetry; only feedback you send is ever transmitted." The Settings footer echoes it ("No accounts, no telemetry. Your words stay private — on your iPhone, or in Apple's private cloud."), and the Help screen's Privacy section reiterates this as: "Transcripts are stored locally on your device. Jot has no cloud sync, no analytics, no account," followed by the single stated exception: when the user taps Send Feedback, their message and any attached screenshots are sent to Jot's feedback endpoint and nothing else the user says or writes ever leaves the device. The only user-initiated outbound transmission in the app is this feedback submission (see §9.6 Feedback Contact); separately, the Donations card makes a read-only network fetch of live totals and charity info, carrying no user data.

chunks.title: Natural-Language Q&A
chunks.text: Natural-Language Q&A. The user asks a plain-language question ("what did I decide about the launch date?", "summarise my notes from last week") and Ask Jot returns a written answer drawn from the user's own transcripts — not generic knowledge. The answer streams in as it's written; while it's preparing, a short status line cycles through "Searching your notes…", "Reading N notes…" once the search lands, then light "thinking" messages until the first words arrive. The field shows no canned example prompts — the user asks their own thing.

chunks.title: Voice or Typed Questions
chunks.text: Voice or Typed Questions. Ask is voice-first: opening it starts listening immediately (without raising the keyboard), so the default action is simply to talk, with a "Listening…" prompt shown until the first words are transcribed. The live transcript fills the question field as the user speaks; tapping the field switches to typing instead (and discards the in-progress voice). The dictated question reuses Jot's own recording + transcription pipeline but is treated as a query only — it is never saved as a transcript. The question field grows to several lines for longer questions. The user can finish and send at any time by tapping the Send button (which doubles as the dictation stop), but they don't have to: once they have actually started speaking, five seconds of silence auto-sends the question — the same finish-and-ask action as the button. During that silence a small "Sending in Ns…" countdown appears below the field (where "Listening" sat); speaking again hides it and resets the timer, so a natural pause between thoughts never sends early. While listening with the field still empty, a rotating, non-interactive suggestion cycles below the "Listening" prompt — example questions phrased as things to say aloud (summarizing the day, asking about a topic, surfacing connected notes) that hint at what retrieval can do and help the user find their voice. The suggestion lingers a few seconds after the first words land, then fades so it never competes with the live transcript.

chunks.title: Cited Answers
chunks.text: Cited Answers. Answers carry inline citation chips that map back to the specific transcripts the answer drew from. Tapping a citation dismisses the Ask sheet and opens that note in Transcript Detail. A sources list beneath the answer shows which transcripts were read, with an attribution line naming Apple's Private Cloud Compute as the model and noting the exchange is private and never stored. For most questions the sources are the notes the model retrieved while answering; for a pure date summary ("summarize last week") they are the notes in that window, cited inline.

chunks.title: Library-Wide Retrieval
chunks.text: Library-Wide Retrieval. Ask searches the user's entire library — including notes captured from the keyboard, Apple Watch, and Shortcuts. Every note is indexed in the iPhone's Spotlight index the moment it is saved (the same index that makes notes findable from the Home Screen — §1.3), and Ask's model searches that index itself while answering — by meaning, by keyword, and by date — so relevant notes surface even when the wording differs and there is nothing for the user to index, download, or wait for. Date-style questions ("yesterday", "last 3 days", "May 26") are resolved by recording time: a pure date summary reads every note in the window in order, while a date plus a topic ("pricing last week") searches within the window.

chunks.title: Answer Model
chunks.text: Answer Model. Ask answers with Apple's Private Cloud Compute — the server-side Apple Intelligence model, chosen for the larger context and stronger synthesis a question across many notes needs — and there is no model choice for the user to make. Nothing is downloaded and Jot runs no server of its own; see §13.1 for what the exchange involves and Apple's privacy guarantees. Ask only surfaces where it can run, so it is never shown in a non-working state (see §14.6).

chunks.title: Availability
chunks.text: Availability. The home Ask entry point appears only on iOS 27, on an iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence, while Apple's per-account daily allowance for Private Cloud Compute is not used up — so Ask is never surfaced in a non-working state. It also depends on Apple having granted Jot access to Private Cloud Compute (Apple grants it to an app by request); until that is in place the entry point stays hidden on every iPhone and the Siri phrase answers "Ask isn't available in this version of Jot yet." On iOS 26 there is no Ask. If the sheet is open when Ask becomes unavailable, it explains what is needed rather than failing silently: Apple Intelligence off or still setting up (with an Open Settings button), an unsupported iPhone, or today's allowance used up (with a See options button that opens Apple's upgrade choices — the allowance resets daily, and iCloud+ raises it). Ask needs a network connection; offline, sending a question reports that plainly.

chunks.title: How-To Answers About Jot
chunks.text: How-To Answers About Jot. Ask also answers questions about how to use Jot itself — "how do I pause a recording?", "does the keyboard have a normal layout?", "what is Warm Hold?" — not only questions about the user's own notes (§14.1). Ask's model decides which kind of question was asked: it can look up Jot's built-in help as well as search the user's notes, and reaches for whichever the question needs — the user never has to pick a mode. A help answer is plain, practical guidance with no citation chips (there is no personal note to point at), and it carries a small "From Jot's Help" label so it is never mistaken for an answer drawn from the user's own notes. The help knowledge is built into the app; the lookup runs through the same Private Cloud Compute session as any other Ask question. For the browsable version of the same material, see the in-app Help screen.

chunks.title: Ask from Shortcuts
chunks.text:
Ask from Shortcuts. Beyond the in-app sheet, Ask is reachable from the Shortcuts app via the "Ask Your Notes" action: ask a question and get a spoken-style answer drawn from your notes, without opening Jot. The answer is plain prose with no citation chips — that surface has nowhere to show them.
